home.heroText: Laghman with hand-pulled noodles, polo from the kazan, lamb from the charcoal grill. All halal, all made in our kitchen.
home.firstTimeText: Uyghur cooking comes from Xinjiang in western China, on the old Silk Road. It has noodles and wok from one side, pilaf, kebab and dumplings from the other. If it is new to you, order these three.

1.title: Laghman
1.text: Wheat noodles pulled by hand, with lamb, peppers, tomato and celery.

2.title: Polo
2.text: Rice with lamb, carrots and raisins, cooked in the kazan.

3.title: Shish kebab
3.text: Cubed lamb over charcoal, with cumin and chili.

home.craftTitle: Dough in the morning, noodles to order
home.craftText: The laghman dough is kneaded in the morning and rests until midday. It is only pulled once the order comes in. Manti and chüchüre are folded by hand. The kebab goes from the grill straight to the table.

craftPoints.1: Dough fresh every day, no ready-made products
craftPoints.2: Lamb and chicken from halal-certified suppliers

home.cultureTitle: Kashgar, Ürümqi and Turpan on the walls
home.cultureText: The fabrics on the columns are ikat from Xinjiang, the caps are called doppa. The pictures show the Heytgah mosque in Kashgar, Ürümqi below the Tianshan and the ruins of Turpan. Tea comes first, ordering comes after.
home.sharingText: Dapanji for two to three people, mixed grill for two, göshnan cut in wedges. For groups of nine or more we put a menu together.
home.visitText: A few minutes from Winterthur main station.

about.title: About us
about.lead: Karahan is a Uyghur restaurant in Winterthur. We cook what Uyghur families cook: noodles, lamb, vegetables, rice and tea.
about.whyText1: The Uyghurs live in Xinjiang in western China, on the old Silk Road. Their cooking joins noodles and wok from the east with pilaf, kebab and dumplings from Central Asia. It is halal, seasoned with cumin and chili, and uses a lot of fresh vegetables.
about.whyText2: In Switzerland this cuisine has hardly existed so far. The name Karahan goes back to the Karakhanids, a dynasty that ruled from Kashgar in the 10th century.

1.title: Dough
1.text: Laghman is pulled, manti and chüchüre are folded, samsa and göshnan are baked. Fresh every day.

2.title: Spices
2.text: Cumin and chili at the grill. Star anise, coriander and saffron in soups and tea.

3.title: Halal
3.text: Meat from halal-certified suppliers. No pork, no alcohol in the food.

4.title: At the table
4.text: Big plates go in the middle. Tea comes first.

kashgar.title: Kashgar
kashgar.text: Oasis city on the western edge of the Taklamakan desert. Known for the Heytgah mosque, the Sunday market and the tea houses. Laghman and samsa come from here.

urumqi.title: Ürümqi
urumqi.text: Capital of Xinjiang, at the foot of the Tianshan mountains. Dapanji, the big plate of chicken, is the city's best-known dish.

turpan.title: Turpan
turpan.text: An oasis 150 metres below sea level, the hottest region of China. Grapes, raisins, melons. The raisins in polo traditionally come from here.
